title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-5
content:
Context:
- Regression observed on 2026-01-14 after runtime PR #512 landed (related to batching internals + kv-cache refactor).
- Symptoms: overall token throughput dropped ~40% on prod host pools for the small-request workload (short seq lengths, many concurrent requests). Baseline before change: ~12k tokens/s per A100. After change: ~6.5k tokens/s.
- Latency: p95 increased from ~55ms -> ~160ms. p99 sometimes spikes >500ms. Error rate unchanged.
- Affected routing: hosted-api region-us-west and dedicated-dev pools. Not all models show same drop (longer-seq model throughput less impacted).

Timeline / quick timeline:
- 2026-01-13: PR #512 merged (batcher refactor + kv-cache allocation changes).
- 2026-01-14 02:00 UTC: alerts for throughput drop.
- 2026-01-14 02:10 UTC: rollback candidate considered, but we tried config tweaks first.
- 2026-01-14 04:00 UTC: rolled back KV cache change in canary -> improvement visible in canary.

What I’ve tried (commands + notes):
1) Inspect batcher logs on a pod (prod canary):
   kubectl -n infra logs deploy/serving-batcher -c batcher --tail=500 | sed -n '1,200p'
   Observed WARN/ERROR lines: 
     "WARN batcher: pending queue length 512 > threshold 256"
     "ERROR batcher: flush timeout after 80ms (pending=32)"
   Interpretation: requests waiting for batch flush for timeout rather than filling optimal batch size.

2) Check current env on deployment:
   kubectl -n infra get deploy serving-runtime -o yaml | yq '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env'
   Key envs: REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX_SIZE=64, REDWOOD_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=20, CONTINUOUS_BATCHING_ENABLED=true, REDWOOD_KV_WARMUP=true

3) Quick experiment: increase batch timeout:
   kubectl -n infra set env deployment/serving-runtime REDWOOD_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=80 
   kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/serving-runtime
   Result (observed after warm-up): throughput rose from ~6.5k -> ~11k tokens/s, p95 increased slightly to ~120ms.
   Note: this suggests too-aggressive timeout was flushing small batches.

4) Toggled KV warmup off on canary:
   kubectl -n infra set env deployment/serving-runtime REDWOOD_KV_WARMUP=false
   rollout restart -> canary throughput improved ~ +15%.
   Hypothesis: KV warmup path introduced CPU/lock contention on short-req workload.

5) Replayed load locally with loadgen (short sequences) + debug build:
   python tools/loadgen.py --reqs 10000 --concurrency 128 --seq-dist short --model redwood/open-7b
   Observed worker CPU saturation in preproc stage (tokenizer).

6) Grepped repo for changes in PR #512:
   git show --pretty=oneline --name-only 512 | cat
   Files: batcher/*, kv_cache/*, threading/pool.py changes (reduced pool size default).

Important log snippets (copied raw):
- "2026-01-14T02:03:12.345Z WARN batcher: pending queue length 512 > threshold 256 (pod=serving-batcher-7c9d)",
- "2026-01-14T02:03:12.426Z ERROR batcher: flush timeout after 80ms (pending=24)\n  stacktrace: batcher.py:line 214 flush_pending -> TimeoutError: batch flush timed out",
- "2026-01-14T02:07:55.112Z INFO kv_cache: warming keyset (estimated=1.2GB) -> started",
- "2026-01-14T02:08:00.987Z ERROR threading.pool: worker-12 crashed: AssertionError: shard_count mismatch (expected 16 got 8)"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Misconfigured batch timeout + smaller batch sizes: REDWOOD_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS was set too low (20ms). On short requests that arrive sporadically, this causes many small flushes -> throughput loss. Evidence: increasing to 80ms improved throughput.
2) Thread pool default reduction in PR #512 reduced parallelism of preproc/tokenization and kv-cache warmup, causing CPU bottleneck. Evidence: worker crashes and CPU saturation in preproc when replaying load.
3) KV cache warmup path introduced locks or blocking IO leading to head-of-line blocking in batcher threads. Evidence: toggling REDWOOD_KV_WARMUP off helps canary.
4) Sequence length distribution shift (client traffic change) means ideal batch size tuning different. Need to compare histograms.
5) Regression exposes an edge case in continuous batching algorithm (combination of small batch threshold + kv-cache warmup) causing internal backpressure.

Quick experiments & measured numbers:
- Baseline (pre-PR): 12k tokens/s (A100), p95 55ms.
- After PR w/ REDWOOD_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=20: 6.5k tokens/s, p95 160ms.
- After bumping REDWOOD_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=80: ~11k tokens/s, p95 ~120ms.
- After disabling REDWOOD_KV_WARMUP on canary: +10-15% throughput improvement vs same timeout setting.

Repro steps to run locally/on canary: (ordered)
1) Deploy canary with PR512 code + toggles:
   kubectl -n infra set image deployment/serving-runtime serving-runtime=myimage:pr512-canary
   kubectl -n infra set env deployment/serving-runtime REDWOOD_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=80 REDWOOD_KV_WARMUP=false
   kubectl -n infra rollout status deployment/serving-runtime
2) Run controlled loadgen (short seq):
   python tools/loadgen.py --reqs 20000 --concurrency 256 --seq-dist short --model redwood/open-7b --report-interval 30
3) Capture metrics: console dashboard route throughput, batcher metrics (pending_queue_length, flushes_by_timeout, avg_batch_size), pod CPU/IO.

Immediate mitigation applied in prod (2026-01-14):
- Increased REDWOOD_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS from 20->80 globally for affected pools.
- Temporarily disabled KV warmup in prod for small-req routing.
- Rolled back PR512 in one cluster where canary indicated revert improved tail latencies.

Open questions / things to verify:
- Are there any clients that rely on low-latency (20ms) correctness and will be harmed by higher batch timeout? Need to check SLOs for latency-sensitive customers.
- Why did PR512 change thread pool default? Was that intentional for memory reasons? PR notes mention kernel selection changes.
- Need histogram of incoming seq lengths per route pre/post change (ask telemetry).
- Check GC/alloc patterns in preproc after PR512 (heap profiles).

Next steps (action items):
- (Aisha) Reproduce on a dedicated perf job with instrumentation: enable detailed batch telemetry (batch_size, wait_ms, flush_reason) -> perf-job id: perf/throughput-reg-2026-01-20.
- (Daniel) Add guard in batcher: if pending_queue > X -> temporarily increase timeout / trigger background aggregator.
- (Maya) Roll a targeted patch to make REDWOOD_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS dynamic based on running avg batch fill rate.
- Add e2e test for small-req workload to CI: assert avg batch size >= 8 under short-req dist.
- Follow up PR: revert the thread-pool default change or make it configurable via env.

Notes / miscellaneous: 
- Related tickets: JIRA INF-3421 (root cause investigation), INF-3424 (perf regression rollout), INF-3430 (canary revert).
- Related PRs: runtime PR#512 (batcher + kv-cache refactor), runtime PR#515 (hotfix for batch flush).
- Slack thread: #eng-serving-runtime thread started by @daniel (link above).

If we need a one-liner for incident timeline / pager: "Throughput regression on short-seq workload caused by batching timeout + KV warmup interactions after PR#512; mitigated by increasing batch timeout and disabling KV warmup, follow-up required to make batching adaptive and revert thread-pool default."
